newsitem.title: USA: Republicans to press balanced-budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Republicans to press balanced-budget amendment.

text.p: Senate Republicans said Saturday they will push for passage of a balanced-budget constitutional amendment without provisions sought by President Clinton that they claimed would weaken it.

In the party's official response to the president's weekly radio address, Maine Sen.-elect Susan Collins said: "The president's version sounds like a fishnet with more holes than rope. We need to pass a strong version of the amendment."

Last week Clinton said he could live with an amendment to the U.S. Constitution requiring a balanced budget if it provided for exceptions when the economy was in recession. Later, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the president still strongly opposed any balanced budget amendment.
Collins chided the administration for sending mixed signals.
"My Republican colleagues and I welcome signals from the White House, however mixed they may be, that the president may finally be changing his mind on the balanced budget amendment," she said.

The November election made passage of the balanced budget amendment likely now that the Republican majority in the Senate has been widened. It had failed in the Senate by one vote. If the amendment clears Congress on the required two-thirds vote of each chamber, it will have to be ratified by three-fourths of the state legislatures.
The president does not have veto power over proposed changes to the U.S. Constitution.
